capabilities: Flat collection repeats a fixed operation count; linear collection increases count by a fixed step.
Total measurement target excludes warmup and calibration. Counts round upward to whole operations; actual duration can exceed the target.
Auto chooses linear when its minimum increasing sequence fits within twice the target, otherwise flat; Airbug also requires the sequence to fit its iteration cap.
Per-case settings inherit by field and explicit CLI options override them. Fixed operation counts skip calibration.
Airbug min/max workload budgets include calibration and warmup; optional external-time exclusion changes budget accounting, not custom measurement values.
native_differences: Criterion doubles warmup batches and estimates operation cost from cumulative elapsed wall time divided by cumulative iterations. Airbug doubles calibration batches to the per-sample target/cap, uses the final calibrated raw interval, then warms up that batch.
Criterion defaults to auto sampling. Airbug defaults to flat; auto is explicit.
Airbug exact integer scheduling and explicit iteration caps replace upstream floating-point planning without an iteration cap.
Airbug rejects exhausted calibration budgets and records achieved sample counts. Neither library promises a hard interruption inside a user operation.
Quick adaptive sampling is a separate policy and is not covered by this audit.
sampling_semantic_audit.validation: All 12 sampling unit tests passed with --offline --locked --all-features on macOS. Integration and external Cargo evidence is referenced individually; this is not a fresh platform-wide gate.

shared_capabilities: Starts with one operation and doubles successive batches without a separate warmup phase.
Stops after minimum elapsed time when adjacent-batch residual falls below a relative target, or at maximum elapsed time.
A user operation is allowed to finish; maximum time is checked between batches rather than interrupting work.
native_differences: Airbug generalizes the residual formula to the actual count ratio, so it also works after reaching its iteration cap.
Airbug keeps every real batch; Criterion keeps only the last pair. For a first batch exceeding the deadline, Airbug retains one sample; Criterion duplicates it with next_up for plotting.
Criterion uses configured Measurement values for residual stability. Airbug uses the reported wall-duration channel, keeping custom metric values independent.
Airbug quick relative-deviation is independent from hypothesis significance; Criterion uses significance_level as the stopping target.
Airbug uses inclusive min/max boundaries and supports separate workload min/max budgets, with maximum budget taking precedence.
quick_semantic_audit.interpretation: Residual stability is an adaptive stopping heuristic, not confidence or significance evidence. Stored sampling.mode identifies quick_adaptive; no exact sampling-distribution equivalence is claimed.
quick_semantic_audit.validation: All seven quick integration tests passed with --offline --locked --all-features on macOS.

capabilities: Register plain operations and shared borrowed inputs without requiring Clone or static lifetime.

native_differences: Criterion bench_function/bench_with_input execute through group run_bench immediately. Airbug registration is lazy and execution happens through Suite::main/run_selected.

Criterion with_filter replaces the current filter and parses regex. Airbug ordinary filters are substrings; Selection::with_regex and CLI --regex provide regex matching. Multiple CLI positive filters form a union, then exclusions apply.
Reject-all is expressible as an exclusion matching every case. Airbug measurement reports an empty-selection error; list/dry-run allow no cases.
Criterion parameter identity uses BenchmarkId; Airbug uses full slash paths and parameter metadata, retaining shared-input and fresh-setup distinctions.

contracts: Sample count controls collected observations; calibration and warmup calls do not become sample observations or throughput work totals.
Warmup runs against wall elapsed time; zero skips warmup. General min/max budgets account for calibration and warmup as separately documented.
Per-field group/case inheritance and explicit overrides preserve zero/false values. Zero samples disables a case before workload execution.
native_differences: Criterion sample_size accepts usize >= 10; Airbug uses u64 and supports 1..9, with zero disabling a case. Airbug defaults to 30 samples versus Criterion 100.
Criterion requires nonzero warmup and defaults to 3 seconds. Airbug permits zero and defaults to 50 milliseconds.
Neither warmup duration nor sample count alone establishes measurement accuracy. The default policies trade collection time differently; use explicit settings for matched experiments.
Airbug calibration precedes its warmup and uses the final calibrated interval; Criterion derives cost from cumulative warmup. Scheduling differences are recorded in sampling_semantic_audit.
